content: What marks Christians attuned to cross-cultural missions? They may not serve as full-time missionaries, but they embrace Great Commission responsibilities. The history of missions reveals little-known senders who used their vocations for strategic gospel advance around the world. Captain Benjamin Wickes (1746–1830) was one such man. ‘Old Captain Wickes’ We meet this early American captain of a merchant vessel unexpectedly at a prayer meeting in 1806. The missionaries in Serampore, India, had gathered to send Henry Martyn to a station on the Ganges River where he would begin his work of translation and evangelism. Martyn recorded that they “met at my pagoda this evening for the purpose of commending me to the grace of God before my departure. My soul never before had such divine enjoyment” ( The Letters of Henry Martyn , 194). I would love to have been there. The meeting included both Baptist missionaries — William Carey, Joshua Marshman, and William Ward — as well as evangelical Anglicans David Brown, Daniel Corrie, and Henry Martyn. It represented a substantial collaboration between these earliest English missionaries for the advance of the gospel in India. Since much of India was controlled by the British East India Company, only Anglican missionaries received official recognition and freedom to travel. Even they, however, could pursue missionary work only when not employed in chaplaincy duties to English people residing in India. Amid such challenges, this prayer meeting of gathered co-laborers was a high point for Martyn and a moment he remembered fondly. To the list of those present, Martyn added “old Captain Wickes.” He mentioned him again in another letter as “the good old Captain Wickes, who has brought out so many missionaries to India” ( Letters , 178). But who was this old American captain so well loved by the English missionaries in India? Missionaries as Risky Passengers Captain Wickes was born to a seafaring family in Maryland in 1746. His older brother, Captain Lambert Wickes, fought and died at sea during the American War for Independence. Benjamin first entered the missionary record in 1799, when the Baptist missionaries Joshua Marshman and William Ward sought passage to India from London. The situation was sensitive. The East India Company had forbidden full-time missionaries from entering, so no English ship would give Marshman and Ward passage. Carey had established his home in the Danish port of Serampore, not far from Calcutta, but no Danish ships were available. Wickes’s American ship, however, could take the risk of transporting missionaries. When he heard about the situation, Wickes wrote to Baptist leader Andrew Fuller, saying that “he had long cherished the hope of being privileged to convey the messengers of the Gospel to the heathen, and that his fondest wish was about to be gratified” ( The Life and Times of Carey, Marshman, and Ward , 110). The privilege came with difficulties. Although American ships were regularly received in East India Company ports, the presence of missionaries complicated their arrival. When Wickes arrived in Calcutta with Marshman and Ward, East India Company officials refused him permission to sail home unless he took the missionaries with him. By God’s grace, Wickes convinced the authorities of the missionaries’ good intentions. When similar circumstances occurred in 1806, he persuaded officials that detaining his American ship might cause an international incident. Each voyage involved protracted negotiations that certainly distracted from his primary trading business. Yet Wickes’s service proved invaluable. Every time the missionaries mentioned him, they affirmed their unbridled thanks for his efforts. William Carey wrote about him in 1805, “I, in common with my dear brethren and sisters here, feel much pleasure in hearing of the safe return to you of our much beloved brother in Christ, Capt. Wickes” ( Evangelical Intelligencer , 1:201). Marshman and Ward called him “th

基督徒如何适应跨文化任务? 他们可能不是全职的传教士,而是承担大委员会的责任。 特派团的历史揭示了鲜为人知的发送者,他们利用自己的使命在世界各地进行战略福音宣传。 Benjamin Wickes上尉(1746–1830)就是这样的人。

威克船长 在1806年的一次祈祷会中,我们意外地遇到了这位早期的美国商船船长. 印度塞兰波尔的传教士们聚集一堂,将亨利·马蒂恩送往恒河上的一个站,在那里他将开始翻译和福音派的工作.

Martyn记录说,他们“今晚在我的佛塔相会,目的是在我离开之前赞扬我受到上帝的恩惠。 我的灵魂从未有过如此神圣的享受”(The Letters of Henry Martyn, 194). 我很想去过那里。

与会的有浸信会传教士威廉·凯里(William Carey),约书亚·马什曼(Joshua Marshman)和威廉·沃德(William Ward)等,还有福音派圣公会教徒大卫·布朗(David Brown),丹尼尔·科里(Daniel Corrie)和亨利·马蒂恩. 它代表了这些最早的英国传教士为在印度推进福音而进行的实质性合作。

由于印度大部分地区被英国东印度公司所控制,只有英国圣公会传教士才得到官方的承认并享有出行的自由. 然而,即使他们也只能在不受雇于居住在印度的英国人担任牧师职务时才能从事传教工作。

在这样的挑战中,这次聚集的同实验室的祈祷会是马蒂恩的高潮,也是他亲切回忆的一瞬. 在出席者名单中,马蒂恩加上了“威克船长”。 他在另一封信中再次提到他,称他为“威克船长,他把这么多传教士带到了印度”(信件,178)。

但这位老美国队长 在印度的英国传教士这么爱谁? 传教士作为"冒险乘客""威克船长"于1746年生于马里兰的一个航海家庭. 他的哥哥,船长兰伯特·威克斯(Lambert Wickes)在美国独立战争中出战并死于海上.

本杰明于1799年首次入传教记录,当时浸信会传教士约书亚·马什曼和威廉·沃德从伦敦寻求通向印度. 情况很敏感。 东印度公司曾禁止全职传教士入道,因此英国船只不会给马什曼和沃德通过.

凯里在离加尔各答不远的丹麦塞兰波尔港建立了他的家,但是没有丹麦船只可供使用. 但威克斯的美国船可能承担运送传教士的风险。

当Wickes听说情况时,他写信给浸信会领袖Andrew Fuller,称“他长期以来一直珍视着有幸将福音信使传达给异教徒的希望,而且他最亲切的愿望即将得到满足”(The Life and Times of Carey, Marshman, and Ward, 110.). 特权带来了困难。

虽然美国船只经常被接收到东印度公司港口,但传教士的到来使其更加复杂. 当威克斯与马什曼和沃德一起到达加尔各答后,东印度公司官员拒绝他出航回家,除非他带着传教士一起. 在上帝的恩典下,威克说服了传教士的善意权威.

当1806年发生类似情况时,他劝说官员们,扣留他的美国船只可能造成国际事件. 每次航行都涉及旷日持久的谈判,当然分散了他的初级贸易业务。 但威克斯的服务证明是宝贵的。 每逢传教士提到他,他们都申明他们无所顾忌地感谢他的努力.

title_zh: 邪恶如何运作
content: Audio Transcript What does evil look like? And sound like? And feel like? Is evil like a horror film set in a haunted forest in a remote cabin at night with floorboards creaking under uninvited footsteps? Or is evil the most scandalous murder trial in the headlines? Is evil more quiet, like in white-collar crimes and embezzlement? Or is it a bloody civil war? There are many forms evil can take. But at its core, how evil works is more essential than all those things I just described. Today on Ask Pastor John: how evil works. This week in our Bible reading, we come upon a trio of texts that collectively reveal to us Satan’s multifront assault — how he works in this world. He is a spiritual deceiver of minds, he is a prosecuting accuser in the heavenly courtroom, and he is a behind-the-scenes influence in human rebellion. He seems to work in a lot of different ways. In John 8 we see him as a liar and murderer. In 2 Peter 2–3 we see him as the deceiver and destroyer. And in Job 4–6 we see him as the provocateur and accuser. Those roles help reveal his work to us in the world. And as we rehearse these roles in our Bible reading this week, we have this email from an anonymous young man. “Pastor John, when I think about spiritual warfare, I often first think about physical things like illness and addiction and even demonic possession. But I wonder if I am missing a larger picture. How much influence does Satan have in this world, and how does he use it? How much of his power is physical? How much of it is unseen? And where do you see him most at work in our modern culture? Is it in obvious sins? Or in subtler ways to keep people from the gospel? How can I see his work without getting preoccupied with him?” A great question with clear purpose. Here’s how Pastor John answered this very question from a young man named Josh in 2018. How Satan Works The word Satan is a transliteration of the Hebrew Satan (śāṭān) and basically means “opponent” or “adversary.” The Greek translation of the Hebrew Old Testament always translates Satan with diabolos in Greek, which means “devil”; we always translate diabolos in English, in the New Testament, “devil.” And diabolos puts a more specific focus on the meaning of the opponent or adversary because diabolos basically means “slander” or “accuse.” It’s used not only to refer to the devil; several times in the Pastoral Epistles of Paul, it’s used to refer to people who are slandering others, speaking evil of them, being false about them. So, even though this supernatural being, this fallen angel and archenemy of God, has a remarkable power in the material or physical realm — he can make people sick, he can throw them in prison, he can even kill them — nevertheless, his main way of opposing God and destroying God’s people is not in the physical or material realm but in the mental or intellectual or moral realm. In other words, the best way to think about his power is not in terms of physical strength but moral deception. Let me try to illustrate this from the Bible. Here’s the passage that piles up more designations of Satan than any other passage in the Bible. If you need one or two verses to put the identity and work of Satan before you, it would be Revelation 12:9–10. Here it says, “And the great dragon was thrown down, that ancient serpent.” And remember what the Bible said in Genesis 3:1 about him. He’s subtler than every beast. So, it’s his subtlety that’s being focused on in his serpent-like reality. “[He] is called the devil [diabolos: slanderer, liar, cheat] and Satan [adversary], the deceiver of the whole world” (Revelation 12:9). I don’t think you can say anything more sweeping or more basic than Revelation 12:9–10. “The accuser of our brothers has been thrown down, who accuses them day and night before our God” (Revelation 12:10). So, at the center of Satan’s purpose is to deceive on earth and to accuse in heaven. If he can deceive you about God and Christ, you will perish. If he can successfu

但从核心上讲,邪恶是如何起作用的 比我刚才描述的那些事情更重要。 今天在"问约翰牧师:邪恶是如何起作用的"上. 这个星期,我们阅读圣经时,看到一连串的文本,这些文本集体向我们揭示了撒旦的多面攻击——他是如何在这个世界上工作的。

title_zh: 你就不能爱所有人吗？
content: “Love one another.” This is one of the undeniable imperatives of Christianity. God is love (1 John 4:8, 16). We must love one another (1 John 4:11). By this love all men know that we are Christ’s disciples (John 13:35). Love fulfills the law (Romans 13:10). So why not just love one another? Why build walls, make distinctions, establish boundaries, and draw lines? Why confront sins? Why not welcome all equally? Can ’ t you just love everyone? The impulse and the argument “just to love everyone” is superficially attractive, even apparently compelling. However, the argument uses Bible language the way Satan does — selectively and deceptively. When tempting Christ, the devil selectively quoted Scripture but twisted the whole sense (cf. Matthew 4:5–7; Psalm 91:11–12). It is possible to use Bible language while ignoring the context, imposing a different meaning on the words and drawing false conclusions based on faulty assumptions. This regularly happens with the meaning of love . Does it really matter? Yes . Churches are disrupted and even destroyed by the confusion created by such shallow reading and reasoning. The language of love is thoroughly scriptural, but we need to handle our Bibles carefully. We need to understand the true definition and the proper direction and order of love. Love Defined and Established Think of love’s definition and foundation. Love does not appear in a vacuum, a sort of glowing, amorphous cloud of feeling which we can press into any mold. Rather, God defines it carefully. God’s love sets the standard for our love: In this the love of God was made manifest among us, that God sent his only Son into the world, so that we might live through him. In this is love, not that we have loved God but that he loved us and sent his Son to be the propitiation for our sins. Beloved, if God so loved us, we also ought to love one another. (1 John 4:9–11) God’s love, which we reflect and replicate by the Spirit’s power, is not a generic niceness but a determined act of the divine will, directed toward the utterly unlovely. It does not at all diminish or dilute the reality of sin. It faces sin’s pollution, punishment, and power head-on, fully honoring divine justice as well as divine mercy. It is love manifested in sacrifice, love determined to do heavenly good to its object, to make the unlovely lovely through whatever righteous means necessary. Christian people show a similar Godlike and Christlike love toward one another. Anticipating his sacrifice, our Lord says, A new commandment I give to you, that you love one another: just as I have loved you, you also are to love one another. By this all people will know that you are my disciples, if you have love for one another. (John 13:34) Christlike love for other believers is a mark of a true disciple. Because God in Christ sets the standard for what love looks like, we cannot collapse Christian love into mere sentimentality, a kind of anodyne sweetness that overlooks or dismisses sin and downplays righteousness. Love Directed and Ordered Think also of love’s direction and order. Our love for our brothers demonstrates our love for God himself (1 John 4:20–21). Our Lord goes to the cross for his beloved people out of love to his Father. The structure of the greatest commandment reveals both direction and order: First , love the Lord your God entirely, and second , love your neighbor as yourself (Matthew 22:37–40; Mark 12:29–31). While not denying a proper love of affinity, Christ calls us to a crowning love of supremacy: We are to love Christ more than father or mother, son or daughter (Matthew 10:37). Love for our nearest and dearest might even be considered hatred in comparison to the love that we have for him (Luke 14:26)! We must not, then, think of love first in its horizontal dimension toward men. Love must first be directed vertically toward God, in response to his love to us, before it spills over horizontally toward others. “Love” toward men at the expense of love t

“彼此相爱。” 这是基督教不可否认的当务之急之一。 上帝是爱(1约翰4:8,16). 我们必须彼此相爱(1约翰4:11). 我们都是基督的门徒(John 13:35), 爱满足法(罗马语:13:10). 那为什么不只相爱呢? 为什么建造围墙、区分、划定界限和划定界限? 为什么面对罪恶?

为什么不平等地欢迎大家? 你就不能只爱每个人吗? 冲动和“仅仅爱每个人”的论点表面上具有吸引力,甚至显然具有说服力。 然而,这一论点使用与撒旦一样的圣经语言——有选择和欺骗. 当诱惑基督时,恶魔有选择地引用了圣经,但扭曲了整个意义(参见马太福音4:5–7;诗篇91:11–12).

可以同时使用圣经语言而忽略上下文,将不同的含义强加于词上,并根据错误的假设得出错误的结论. 这经常发生在爱的意义。 这真的重要吗? 对 教会被这种浅浅的阅读和推理造成的混乱所扰乱甚至摧毁。

爱的语言是彻头彻尾的文字,但我们需要仔细处理我们的圣经. 我们需要了解真正的定义,以及爱的正确方向和秩序. 爱的定义和基础。 爱情不会出现在真空中, 一种发光的,无形态的感受云, 我们可以压进任何模具。 相反的,上帝是精心定义的。

上帝的爱为我们的爱设定了标准: 在这件事情中,上帝的爱在我们中间被显现出来,上帝把他唯一的儿子送入了世界,以便我们通过他而生存. 爱不是我们爱上帝 而是他爱我们 派他儿子来为我们的罪孽辩护 被爱,如果上帝如此爱我们, 我们也应该相爱。

(1 John 4:9-11)上帝的爱,我们用精神的力量来反映和复制,不是一种一般的善意,而是神意志的坚定行为,直接对准完全不爱的人。 它丝毫没有削弱或淡化罪恶的现实。 它面临着罪恶的污染、惩罚和权力,完全尊重神圣的正义和神圣的慈悲。

爱表现在牺牲中,爱决心为它的目标做天上的好事,通过任何必要的正义手段使不爱的人变得可爱. 基督教徒对彼此的爱 表现出类似上帝和基督的爱

我们的主说,在期待他的牺牲时,我给你新的戒律,即你们彼此相爱:正如我一直爱你们一样,你们也要彼此相爱。 由此一切众生悉知汝等为我弟子,若有相爱. (约翰13:34) 基督爱其他信徒是真正的门徒的标志.

因为上帝在基督中为爱的外表设定了标准, 我们不能把基督教的爱 变成单纯的多愁善感, 一种忽视或否定罪孽和贬低正义的厌倦的甜言蜜语。 Love Directed and Ordered 想想爱的方向和秩序。 我们对我们兄弟的爱显示了我们对上帝本人的爱(1 John 4:20–21).

我们的主为了他敬爱的百姓去十字架 为了他父亲 最伟大的戒律结构揭示了方向和秩序:第一,完全爱主你的神,第二,像爱自己一样爱邻居(Matthew 22:37–40;Mark 12:29–31).

基督在不否认亲情的同时, 要求我们拥有至高无上的爱: 我们比父亲或母亲、儿子或女儿更爱基督(Matthew 10:37)。 相较于我们对他的爱,对亲近和最亲近的爱甚至可能被视为仇恨(公爵14:26)! 那么,我们决不能在对男人的横向层面首先想到爱情。

title_zh: 任务对儿童来说是否太昂贵？
content: Are my children also called to this ? As a mama missionary, I wonder about our fitness for the task when our family of eight clogs airport security and labors in language study and ministry like a well-meaning circus. Will my kids catch a deadly virus from the airport carpet? Will beans be lunch every day ? How can we possibly replace years spent with grandparents and a vibrant children’s church? Will they become healthy adults when this calling cuts not only us but them? Are the unreached regions of the Joshua Project map reserved for singles? Our family’s plane-ticket prices alone might argue that case. Does the church only send the strong? In the world’s economy, our crew is inefficient and slow to get the job done. Risk Worth Reward The missionary call may cost our precious children extra bouts of food poisoning, power outages, awkward cultural moments, and loneliness. It may even, like Perpetua Broten and Ezra, Violet, and Calvin Pals , require their lives. When Jesus called his followers, he asked for painful, costly sacrifice. He reminded them that though foxes and birds return each day to their burrows and nests, he had no place to lay his head (Matthew 8:20). He called his disciples to take no change of clothes or spare coin for their ministry (Matthew 10:9–10). And yet he said, “There is no one who has left house or brothers or sisters or mother or father or children or lands, for my sake and for the gospel, who will not receive a hundredfold” both now and in eternity (Mark 10:29–30). God’s economy is not man’s. Jesus calls kids to go with moms and dads to serve the nations because God’s kingdom advancement is for families too, and the risk is worth its reward. The forward momentum of God’s kingdom does not exclude our children. The garden mandate to be fruitful and multiply now expands spiritually, and we take our kids along. We aren’t disqualified from overseas ministry if we’re changing diapers on the hour. God is the author of life and the genius behind the family design. Our dominion over the earth as image-bearers includes those in our care, even if they look too small to slay dragons. The risks of going with kids in tow are many; only the rewards of trust and obedience eclipse their reality. If we pursued mere adventure or greater cultural appreciation, we would be the “most to be pitied” (1 Corinthians 15:19). But if God calls us to glory in Christ in dungeon-like places, teaching our children to cup their hands around their mouths and cry to prisoners, “Come out!” then we offer them diamond-quality joy (Isaiah 49:9, 61:1). We weep with our kids over the cost they see and feel in their own lives, helping them gather the broken pieces of their hearts to hand to Jesus, teaching them firsthand that Christ’s flesh and blood satisfy. Shepherding Your Flock Before my two oldest children were dunked in the cold mountain water of our village in baptism, they testified to God’s grace in their lives. God had shown them his best at their worst. I flinched inwardly as I heard them recall dangerous accidents and desperate emotions in our time overseas. But when it turned darkest, God shone brightest. If it were up to me, I would have taken an eraser to God’s plan of pain for them. If I had, I would also have unknowingly rubbed out his intimate deliverances. The pleasure of following God to the farthest reaches of the planet with your kids is finding that God is there too. All that said, our family just moved ministry locations overseas due to prolonged isolation and our kids’ growing need for friends and community. Missions is a family affair and worth the risk, while at the same time, God does not depend on our presence in a place to accomplish his purposes, and he cares specifically for our kids. Our kids’ particular needs are not at odds with our calling but can direct our feet and make us wise shepherds of our flock. God is not biting his nails on the sidelines of our missionary service, hoping we’ll perform well enou
content_zh:
我的孩子也被叫来了吗? 作为一位母亲传教士,我想知道我们是否适合完成这项任务,当我们这个8个堵塞的机场保安和劳工家庭在语言学习和像一个善意的马戏团一样的部委工作时。 我的孩子会从机场地毯上感染致命病毒吗? 每天吃豆子吃午饭吗? 我们怎样才能取代在祖父母和充满活力的儿童教堂度过的岁月?

他们会不会成为健康的成年人 当这个呼吁不仅削减我们,而且削减他们? 约书亚计划图中未进入的地区是否为单人保留? 我们家族的飞机票价本身就可能证明这一点。 教会只派强者吗? 在世界经济中,我们的船员效率低下,完成任务的速度缓慢。

值得回报的风险 传教士的召唤可能使我们珍贵的孩子们额外损失食物中毒、断电、尴尬的文化时刻和孤独。 它甚至可能像Perpetua Broten和Ezra、Violet和Calvin Pals一样需要他们的生命。 当耶稣召唤他的追随者时,他要求痛苦,昂贵的牺牲.

他提醒他们,虽然狐狸和鸟儿每天返回他们的洞穴和巢穴,但他没有地方安顿头颅(Matthew 8:20). 他叫门徒们不要为他们的部会换衣服或多余的硬币(Matthew 10:9-10).

然而,他却说,“没有人离开过家,也没有人离开过兄弟姐妹,也没有人离开过母亲、孩子或土地,为了我和福音,现在和永远都得不到一百倍”(Mark 10:29-30)。 上帝的经济不是人类的经济。

因为上帝的王国进步也是为了家庭, 上帝王国的前进势头并不排除我们的孩子。 花园的任务富有成果,倍增,现在精神上有所扩展,我们带着我们的孩子一起走.

如果我们换尿布, 上帝是生命的作者,也是家庭设计背后的天才. 我们作为形象持有者对地球的统治权包括那些受我们照顾的人,即使他们看起来太小,不能杀死龙。 和孩子一起被拖走的风险是很多的;只有信任和服从的回报掩盖了他们的现实。

如果我们仅仅追求冒险或更大的文化欣赏,我们将“最可怜”(科林斯15:19)。 但是,如果上帝在类似地牢的地方召唤我们在基督中荣耀,教我们的孩子用手握住嘴,向囚犯喊叫,“出来吧!”那么我们给他们提供钻石质量的快乐(以赛亚49:9,61:1)。

我们和孩子们一起为他们自己生活中所看到和感受到的代价而哭泣,帮助他们收集心碎的碎片交给耶稣,并亲身教他们基督的血肉满足。 在我两个年长的孩子 被浸在村里的寒冷山水里之前 他们证明了上帝的恩惠

上帝在他们最坏的时候 给他们展示了他最好的一面 当我听到他们回想起我们海外时代的危险事故和绝望情绪时,我内向退缩。 但当它变得最黑暗时,上帝会闪耀 如果由我决定的话,我本来会用一个抹除器去完成上帝给他们的痛苦计划。 如果我有的话,我也会不知不觉地 抹去他的亲切奉献。

和你们的孩子一起跟随上帝到达地球最远的地方的乐趣 就是发现上帝也在那里 我们的家人因为长期孤立和孩子对朋友和社区的日益需求,刚刚将部属迁往海外。

使命是一种家庭事务,值得冒风险,与此同时,上帝并不依赖我们的存在来实现他的目的,他特别关心我们的孩子. 我们的孩子的特殊需求与我们的召唤并不矛盾,

title_zh: 乔尔·斯莫尔伯恩和他的兄弟刚刚制作了一部关于战争兄弟的电影
content: At one point, Joel Smallbone and his brother Ben went their separate ways. “You could argue we ended up on our own sort of opposite sides of life’s battlefield,” Smallbone says. What brought them back together was a movie about the same thing. “I remember saying, wouldn’t it be fascinating if two brothers who’ve had ideological differences and creative differences came back together behind the camera to tell a story about two brothers that end up on opposite sides of a literal war?” That movie is Drummer Boy , a Revolutionary War Christmas musical that opened in theaters Nov. 6. Joel and Ben co-directed it, and Joel plays Jeremiah Clem. The cast includes Ioan Gruffudd and Melora Hardin (Jan from The Office) . It took a while. Smallbone, who sings in for KING + COUNTRY with his brother Luke, pitched it to Lionsgate on March 10, 2020, and, by his account, the studio nearly greenlit it. “And then March the 13th happened and the world shut down,” he says. Unsung Hero came first and the musical waited. Someone eventually reminded him 2026 is America’s 250th birthday. “Well, maybe it was just always meant to be now.” The Movie That Wrote Him “Do you write the movie or does the movie write you?” Smallbone asks. “There’s never been a movie that’s written me more than Drummer Boy .” He lists the evidence. “We came up with this rendition of ‘The Little Drummer Boy’ at the beginning of our career. We’re called for KING + COUNTRY, which is a British mantra. We wore these revolutionary-type uniforms for many years. I’m in a band with my brother. This is a movie about brothers on opposite sides of the battlefield. I’m a musician. It’s a musical. You just see all of these breadcrumbs.” When he got stuck on the lead character, a director asked him who he was. “I’ve got a rescuer complex,” he says. “A bit of a savior complex. And so I just wrote all of it into the film.” Unsung Hero was literally about his family, so it’s fair to ask why this one feels more like him. His answer is allegory. “Jesus was the allegory guy,” Smallbone says. “He made up stories for a living, you know? I see myself more in it because it’s all allegorical about our life, and America, and me being an immigrant and in a mixed marriage, and brothers on other sides of the battlefield.” A Musical for People Who Hate Musicals “I need to clear up something to the musical haters,” he says. About 30 minutes of the film are musical moments, “very personal expressions of heartache or love or loss.” He calls it “ Hamilton meets The Patriot meets Pride and Prejudice .” His rule for when a character should sing is simple. “The best musicals put language to things that you couldn’t express through dialogue. The worst musicals just sing the whole time. And I’m like, just stop. That’s not life.” His example is Chris Martin writing “Fix You” after Gwyneth Paltrow’s father died. “You have to express yourself in grief, in pain, and a lot of times it comes through music.” The same logic runs through the film. One character, an enslaved woman, sings her way through being stuck. “She’s stuck and she’s enslaved and she needs to sing about it to understand it better,” he says. Two Brothers Behind the Camera The shoot gave the co-directing brothers plenty of challenges to overcome. The last day of filming was the big argument between Jeremiah and Emmaline on a hillside, in 40 mph winds. “She’s in this dress, almost getting blown off the hillside,” Smallbone says. “We were like, I don’t know if we’re gonna use any of this.” The wind made the cut. “The tragedy of the bad weather actually created a third layer to the scene.” The argument matters to the story. Jeremiah, Smallbone says, is “not practicing what he’s preached.” His father taught him “no boy or girl or slave or free, because all in one in Christ are we,” an echo of Galatians 3:28. Jeremiah is “chasing, basically, imperialism and hierarchy and climbing the ladder by who he’s gonna marry.” Heat was the opposite problem. On a day he puts

title_zh: 想要帮助消除贫困吗？这里有五种方法可以开始
content: In the mid-2000s, Ate Tina was working long hours at a factory in the Philippines and supporting her household alone. Ate is Tagalog for older sister, and it’s a title of respect. Seven months after her wedding, her husband developed a serious medical condition, which made her the only breadwinner. When she became pregnant, the factory’s demands stayed the same. “I ended up giving birth at home because I wasn’t allowed to leave work,” she recalls. Two months after her daughter was born, she was back on the factory floor and her daughter was in the care of others. Tina began to notice changes in her daughter’s behavior that worried her. She says she prayed in desperation for a livelihood that would let her provide for her family and be present with them. In 2008, she connected with the Center for Community Transformation, a partner of HOPE International in the Philippines. Her first loan was $80. She repaid it, kept meeting with staff and fellow borrowers, and by her third loan, $800, she bought three sewing machines and rented an apartment to start a sewing business. “Because of that trust, I was able to start a business I can call my own,” she says of the organization that lent to her. The business has since grown into an online clothing company with around 70 employees. Tina trains them, encourages them to save and points them toward the same support she found. The loan mattered. So did the parts of her story that cost nothing: people who trusted her, a group of borrowers who met with her, a prayer life she kept returning to and a skill she kept sharpening. If your budget has no room for a monthly gift, that list is still within reach. Here are five places to start: Watch the way you talk about poverty. Poverty is more than a shortage of money. Material need is real, and it sits inside a larger brokenness that reaches into relationships, communities and a person’s sense of who they are. Talking about poverty that way changes who is in the story. Everyone knows what a broken relationship feels like, so the distance between you and the person asking for help on the corner gets shorter. You make eye contact instead of looking away. You ask a name. You find out what the person actually needs before you decide what to offer. Protect the dignity of the people you want to help. Tina put the turning point in terms of trust. The lender believed she would repay, and she did, and the business that followed was hers. That makes a useful test for any help you offer: does it treat a person as someone with ideas and work of their own, or as someone to be rescued? Giving things away freely is the right call in a crisis. Outside a crisis, it can turn people into recipients in their own community. The better question is how to meet someone’s needs as a whole person while protecting their dignity. Do your job well. You don’t have to work for a nonprofit to fight poverty at work. Vocation is one of the main ways Christians answer the call to love their neighbors, which means many of us are already doing some of that work without noticing. Tina’s sewing business now supports around 70 employees, which is vocation doing exactly this. A barista pours coffee grown by farmers in developing countries. Someone in telecommunications works in an industry that provides cell-phone access in impoverished nations. A worker on an oil field produces fuel that keeps a stranger warm at night. A recruiter connects a person to a job that person badly needs. Pray about where you’ve been placed, do the work well, and think of it as a way to serve people you will probably never meet. Spend your time where the need already is. Poverty has an address close to home, too. Food pantries, tutoring programs and church benevolence ministries run on volunteers, and they tend to need people who show up on a schedule. A standing weeknight shift usually builds more trust than a one-time service day, because the people on the other side get to know your name as well. If you have
content_zh:
2000年代中期,Ate Tina在菲律宾的一家工厂工作了很长的时间,独自养活她的家人. Ate是Tagalog的姐姐, 在她结婚七个月后,她的丈夫发展出严重的健康状况,这使她成为唯一的养家糊口的人. 她怀孕后,工厂的要求保持不变。

她回忆道, “我最后在家中分娩, 女儿出生后两个月,她回到了工厂地板上,她的女儿在别人的照顾下. 蒂娜开始注意到她女儿担心自己行为的变化. 她说,她绝望地祈求生计,使她能够养活家人,并与家人同在。

2008年,她与HOPE国际在菲律宾的合作伙伴社区转型中心建立了联系. 她第一次贷款是80美元。 她偿还了这笔钱,不断与员工和同僚借款人会面,通过第三次贷款800美元,她买了三台缝纫机并租了一套公寓来开办缝纫业务.

“由于这种信任,我得以开办一个我可以称为我自己的企业,”她说,是借给她的组织。 该行从此发展为一家有约70名员工的在线服装公司. 蒂娜训练他们,鼓励他们保存并指向她找到的同样支持. 贷款很重要。

她的故事中那些没有付出任何代价的部分也一样: 相信她的人, 一群与她相遇的借款人, 她不断回归的祈祷生活, 以及她不断磨炼的技能。 如果你的预算没有月度礼物的空间,那名单仍然可以拿到. 这里有五个开始的地方: 注意你谈论贫穷的方式。 贫穷不仅仅是缺乏资金。

物质需求是真实的,它存在于更大的断裂之中,这种断裂涉及到关系、社区和一个人对自身身份的感觉。 说到贫穷 那样会改变故事中是谁 每个人都知道一个破碎的关系是什么感觉,所以你和在角落寻求帮助的人之间的距离会缩短. 你用眼睛接触而不是看不见

你问个名. 在你决定要提供什么之前,先找出这个人实际需要什么. 保护你想要帮助的人的尊严。 蒂娜把转折点 以信任。 贷款人相信她会报答她,她会报答她,随后的生意是她的。

这对你提供的任何帮助都是一种有益的考验:它是把一个人当作有想法和工作的人,还是当作要被拯救的人? 在危机中,自由放弃事物是正确的号召。 在危机之外,它可以把人们变成自己社区的受援者。 更好的问题是,如何满足个人整体的需要,同时保护他们的尊严。 做好你们的工作

你不必为非营利组织工作, Vocation是基督徒响应爱邻居号召的主要方式之一,这意味着我们许多人已经在做一些没有注意的工作. 蒂娜的缝纫行业支持大约70名员工, 一个酒吧为发展中国家农民所种植的咖啡倒灌.

电信业的某个人在贫穷国家提供手机接入的行业工作。 油田上的工人生产出能让陌生人在晚上保持温暖的燃料. 招募者将一个人与他急需的工作联系起来。 祈祷自己被安置在何处, 做得很好,

把时间花在需要的地方 贫穷也有一个离家很近的地址。 食物裤、辅导计划和教会慈善部都以志愿者为对象,他们往往需要按期出现。 每周上夜班通常比一次服务日更能建立信任,因为另一边的人也了解你的名字。 如果你有的话

title: Claire Rosinkranz Heard God at 11. Now She’s Learning to Hear Him Differently
summary: Six years after a ukulele song made her a TikTok phenomenon, the pop songwriter is learning to hear God differently — and to be okay living in the middle.
summary_zh: 在一首尤克里里歌曲使她成为TikTok现象的六年后，这位流行歌曲作者正在学习以不同的方式聆听上帝—并且可以在中间生活。
title_zh: 克莱尔·罗辛克兰兹（ Claire Rosinkranz ）在11岁时现在，她正在学会以不同的方式倾听他的声音
content: Claire Rosinkranz is trying to describe what the last few years have felt like, and she keeps landing on the same word: momentum. Not the kind she chased. The kind that showed up on its own, at 16, and never fully let her catch up to it. “It feels really good, honestly it’s kind of hard to understand how it feels at all,” she says backstage at a music festival. “When I was 16 I had a lot of crazy momentum, and I’ve been telling my team, I just didn’t realize anything that was happening. And so I still feel like I don’t know what’s happening. But I get to sing and dance.” “Backyard Boy” turned a California teenager with a ukulele and a home studio into one of pop’s more unlikely breakouts, a song that racked up millions of TikTok recreations before she’d finished high school. Rosinkranz was already a lifer by then. She’d been writing songs since she was 8 and training as a ballerina before deciding, at 11, that music was the thing. Now 22, with two albums behind her, she is still working out what it means to have built a career on momentum she never planned for. “I gotta learn a lot of patience,” she says. The success of that first song, she says, set her expectations in a way she’s been unwinding ever since. “I ended up getting a lot of success from that song, and so all I knew was success when it came to music,” she says. “So feeling that kind of ebb and flow has been a challenge.” The deeper lesson has been separating who she is from what she makes. Someone in her life has been trying to drill it into her that her worth doesn’t live in her output. “My identity is not in what I do, but in who I am,” she says. “That can be really hard when you get compliments and value from everything that you do in this world. I’m still learning that there’s a lot of ebbs and flows in this industry, and learning how to be in the middle of that.” Being in the middle of things is a phrase she comes back to more than once, and it stretches past her career into how she talks about God. She grew up with a faith that felt less like a decision than a default setting. “God was kind of in my nature,” she says. “Religion was a little bit more like taught to me.” The distinction matters to her more now than it used to. She describes a recent conversation with her therapist in which she admitted she doesn’t hear God the way she once did, half expecting to be told something was wrong. “I was like, I feel like I don’t hear God that much or in the way that I used to, and she was like, I actually don’t completely agree,” Rosinkranz says. “I think that you maybe just hear God differently. I really resonated with that.” Lately, she’s been wondering whether the change is less about losing God’s voice than learning its new frequency. “I’m really learning how to be in the middle of a lot of things, and being okay with being a little bit more fluid instead of having this really crazy concept of right and wrong,” she says. “I feel like I’m a little bit more black and white than I would like to acknowledge, and you can’t really have a lot of growth or change if you don’t.” Her spiritual life shows up in practical, almost mundane ways. Yoga, horseback riding, long afternoons at the beach. She talks to God the way other people talk to a friend, and she asks for dreams, treating them as ground she can meditate from. But the clearest version of the story lives in a memory she comes back to whenever she needs to remember why she’s doing any of this. She was 11, in the back of her cousin’s car, weighing a choice between two loves: ballet and music. “I was sitting there and I was like, God, am I gonna do dance or music, because I was also very passionate about ballet,” she says. “I swear that I heard this other voice that wasn’t myself. That is the thing and the voice that has honestly carried me to where I am today.” She went straight to her mother afterward. “I heard God in a way that I haven’t heard before,” she remembers telling her. “It’s really cool to see everything

title_zh: N.T.赖特：基督徒需要一个比我们大多数人所描绘的更大的神
content: N.T. Wright was a boy in a choir singing Handel’s Messiah when Isaiah first got into his head. “Comfort, comfort my people” and “He was wounded for our transgressions” became part of his mental furniture, he says, and the furniture stayed. By his teens he loved the book enough to consider an Old Testament PhD. He chose Romans instead, partly because Paul quotes Isaiah constantly and gave him a lifelong excuse to keep going back. His new book Into the Heart of Isaiah: The Meaning and Message of Isaiah 40-55 is what came of it, a walk through sixteen chapters he calls one of the most extraordinary poems ever written. If they had been dug out of a scroll in the sands of Libya or Jordan, he told RELEVANT, the whole world would put them on the front page. “This is an amazing piece of writing.” Because they sit in the middle of the Old Testament, he says, many readers just think “bit of the Bible, not sure what that’s about.” He reads them three ways: as the ancient Israelites heard them, as Jesus and the apostles used them, and as they speak to the Church now. Starting with the first, Wright says, “gives us a kind of stability to any other interpretations we then come to.” Some of the best-known lines in American Christianity come from these chapters, including “Mount up with wings as eagles” and “No weapon formed against thee shall prosper.” Wright says anyone reaching for that second verse should remember that an enemy may be claiming the same verse for themselves. After all, in the First World War, British and German forces sang some of the same hymns and claimed the same God’s protection. Context helps, he says, even if we never get all of it. These chapters are addressed to a people exiled for their sin and told that God has dealt with it. Read them as a promise about my success, my salvation, a happy marriage or a thriving business, and “that’s not the story that those verses belong to.” God can give those things, he says, usually inside a larger story about belonging to a people sent to the world, which “may involve pain, suffering, renunciation, et cetera, as well as fulfillment. But let’s never imagine that they’re the whole thing.” He starts the exile story with Adam and Eve, the first people sent out of the garden, and says Israel was the people called to rescue the whole human race, which is why exile brought despair. A people in that position needs forgiveness as well as a way home. The center of the passage, as he reads it, is that God, who had left Jerusalem and the temple to their fate, “is coming back himself in person to sort it all out.” The New Testament applies the same words to John the Baptist getting ready for Jesus. War, Money and Sex Asked whether exile describes the Church now, Wright says he is careful. Five centuries ago Martin Luther wrote about the Babylonian captivity of the Church and cast himself as the one leading it home, a story Wright calls a gross oversimplification, one Luther may have come to see as “over-egging the pudding.” Exile follows idolatry, though, so he names the idols he sees: Mars, Mammon and Aphrodite, or war, money and sex. Each one makes demands and shuts down objections. The military needs it, the markets need it, everybody does it. Part of the problem, he says, is that the Western Church “has joined in the worship of war, has joined in the worship of money, has joined in the worship or at least the collusion with erotic love.” He adds that people need money and defense, and that God gave us our erotic selves. “But when you make them idols and when you give them power over you, then as individuals and as a culture and alas as a church, you’re heading for the rocks.” The rebuke he returns to most is about heaven. The idea that Christianity is about a soul going to heaven when it dies, he says, comes from Plato and from writers like Plutarch, a pagan priest, and not from the Bible. “The name of the game in Christianity is that heaven is going to come to earth.” He points to the
content_zh:
N. T. Wright是唱着汉德尔的弥赛亚的合唱团中的一个男孩,当时以赛亚刚入脑. 他说,“安慰我的人,安慰我的人”和“他因我们的过错而受了伤”,成为他精神家具的一部分,家具也留下了。 在他十几岁的时候,他喜欢这本书 足以考虑一个旧约博士。

他选择了罗马人取而代之,部分原因是保罗不断引用以赛亚的话,并给了他终生的借口来继续后行. 他的新书"入以赛亚之心:以赛亚40-55的意义与信息"正是由此而来,他通过16个章节的走来,称这为有史以来最出众的一首诗.

如果从利比亚或约旦的沙子上挖出卷轴,他告诉相关人士,全世界都会把它们放在头版。

“这是一部惊人的著作。” 因为他们坐在《旧约》的中间,他说,许多读者只是认为“圣经的比特词,不知道是什么。 ” 他读了他们三种方式:古代以色列人听到他们,耶稣和使徒使用他们,现在他们向教会说话.

或他们自己。 毕竟,在第一次世界大战中,英国和德军演唱了部分同名颂歌并声称得到同名神的保护. 他说,即使我们永远得不到一切,背景还是有帮助的。 这些章节是针对一个因罪行被放逐的民族的,并告诉上帝已经处理了.

读这些诗句是为了保证我的成功、我的救赎、幸福的婚姻或兴旺的生意,并且“这些诗句不属于这个故事。” 他说,上帝可以给这些东西,通常是在一个关于属于被送到世界的民族的大故事中,“这可能涉及痛苦、痛苦、放弃等等,以及实现。

但让我们永远不要想象, 他以亚当和夏娃为开头的放逐故事,第一批被派出花园的人,并说以色列是被叫来拯救整个人类的人,这就是放逐带来绝望的原因. 处于这种地位的人既需要宽恕,也需要回家。

正如他所读到的,通道的中心是让耶路撒冷和圣殿走向命运的上帝,“正在亲自回来整理一切。” "新约"对浸信会的约翰(John) 准备接受耶稣也适用了同样的话. 战争、金钱和性问题问流亡者是否描述教会,

5个世纪前,马丁·路德(Martin Luther)写了一篇关于巴比伦人对教会的囚禁并把自己当做回家的领头羊,莱特(Wright)称这故事过于简单化,一位路德(Luther)可能已经看成是“过度的布丁了 ” 。 出走虽然跟随偶像,所以取出他所见到的偶像的名字:火星,马蒙和阿佛洛狄忒,或者战争,金钱和性.

每一个都提出要求并关闭反对。 军方需要它,市场需要它,每个人都这样做。 他说,问题的一部分是西方教会“加入了对战争的崇拜,加入了对金钱的崇拜,加入了对金钱的崇拜,或者至少与色情爱相勾结”。 他补充说,人们需要金钱和防卫,上帝给了我们自己的性。

“当你们以偶像为偶像,当你们以个人、文化、教堂为主宰时,你们就走向石头去。” 他回到多数人的责难 是关于天堂的 他说,基督教是关于灵魂去天堂的观念,来自柏拉图和普鲁塔克等作家,是异教牧师,而不是圣经.

“在基督教中,游戏的名称是天堂将降临到地上。” 他说

title_zh: 带上你的圣经和你的霰弹枪：认识有史以来最多的佛罗里达教堂植物
content: Sunday services at TruLife Church of Ocala’s newest campus come with a soundtrack of shotguns going off in the distance. Some attendees bring their own and check them at a rack by the door, the way other congregations check strollers. The campus is called BlackJack, like the range it meets at: Blackjack Sporting Clays, a shooting facility in Sumterville, Fla. The facility’s owners came up with the idea and asked pastor Michael Kirby about starting a church plant on the property. Kirby has a handy comparison for the place, which has four courses and a cart. “You rent a golf cart and you drive around and shoot clays at all the different posts,” he said. “It’s like playing golf, but you’re playing with a shotgun.” So it’s golf, but the clubs go off. The sanctuary, loosely speaking, is a pavilion enclosed in thick, clear plastic, with mobile air conditioners keeping the cool air in and the wooded views visible. An 80-inch TV and a full sound system play Kirby’s prerecorded sermon three weeks a month, so three Sundays out of four the preacher arrives by screen. He or another TruLife pastor preaches live once a month, and Kirby’s daughter-in-law, Taylor Kirby, leads worship. Seating is about 40. The church held a soft opening a couple of months ago and had its official launch on Sunday, Oct. 25, with Kirby preaching and a picnic lunch afterward. The day before, during a national competitive shooting event at the facility, volunteers handed out flyers and went door to door in the neighborhood, which is outreach with an unusually loud backdrop. The target audience is the person who came to shoot. “We are hoping to attract unchurched people who are coming to BlackJack to do some shooting,” Kirby said. “Maybe they wouldn’t want to go to your typical church, but they decide they could go over here under the pavilion and hang out.” Evangelism by proximity, in other words: set up next to the people with the shotguns and hope they wander over. Some of them already have noticed the music. Kirby says shooters have told him they can hear the worship from the service, and he is counting on it. “They might not come inside yet, but they’ll be out there worshipping in the middle of the grass,” he said. The worship set, it turns out, doubles as the range’s ambient soundtrack.
content_zh:
Ocala最新校园的TruLife教堂(TruLife Church), 一些与会者自己带过来,在门边的架子上检查,其他会众检查步行者的方式. 校园被称为BlackJack,就像它所遇见的射程: 黑杰克体育克莱斯(英语:Blightjack Sporting Clays),是位于弗拉州苏姆特维尔的一个射击设施.

该设施的业主想出了这个想法,问牧师Michael Kirby关于在该地产上开办一座教堂工厂的问题。 柯比对该地进行了方便的比较,该地有四门课程和一辆推车. 他说:「你租一辆高尔夫球车, “这就像打高尔夫, 高尔夫球,但俱乐部会爆炸。

松散的说,圣所是一个被厚厚的,清晰的塑料包裹的展厅,移动式空调保持了凉爽的空气,木质的景色也清晰可见. 一个80英寸的电视和一个完整的音响系统每月三个星期播放Kirby预先录制的布道,

他或另一位特鲁利夫牧师每月传教一次,柯比的媳妇泰勒·柯比领头崇拜. 座位约40. 教堂在几个月前举行了软开放,并于10月25日星期日正式开堂,柯比在教堂传教,之后进行野餐午餐.

前一天,在设施举行的全国竞技射击活动中,志愿者们散发了传单,并在附近挨家挨户地挨家挨户地走来挨户走去。 目标观众是前来拍摄的人. Kirby说,“我们希望吸引前来BlackJack进行射击的无伤大雅的人。”

“也许他们不想去你们典型的教堂, 近处的福音主义,换句话说:用猎枪布置在人民旁边,希望他们漫游. 其中一些人已经注意到了音乐。 Kirby说枪手告诉他,他们可以听到仪式上的礼拜,他指望着它。

他说,“他们可能还没有进屋,但会在草丛中崇拜”。 结果发现,这种崇拜是环境音轨的两倍。

title_zh: “Mogging”是柯林斯词典2026年的年度词汇
content: Your friend’s sourdough mogs the loaf you spent all weekend proving. That sentence now has a dictionary’s blessing, because Collins Dictionary has named “mogging” its Word of the Year for 2026. Collins defines it as “outperforming or outshining someone or something, which can mean making them look inferior in appearance, confidence or status.” The word is believed to be short for AMOG, “alpha male of the group.” It started around 2016 in bodybuilding culture, where it named the most physically dominant guy in the gym, then turned into a verb and made the rounds in the manosphere. It’s everywhere now and mostly used with tongue firmly in cheek, which is the only way anyone should use a word that started as a locker-room pecking order. Carspreading made Collins’ list, which is what they call carmakers building vehicles longer, wider and heavier with every new model. SUVs were well over half of new car sales in 2025, and the parking bays are feeling it. The job market contributed ghost job, an opening posted by an employer with no plan to hire anyone. Collins cites a UK study finding that around a third of advertised roles fit the description, so if your applications keep disappearing into the void, that may be part of why. The lighter entries were friendslop, low-budget indie games built for playing with friends, and fricy, fruity plus spicy, as in pineapple and mango hot sauces. Bixie is the haircut between a bob and a pixie that Zendaya, Jessie Buckley and Helen Mirren have worn. Then there is P(doom), the percentage chance someone thinks AI brings about the collapse of human civilization, which is a strange thing to find on the same list as a haircut and a hot sauce. Collins writer Rachel Quin said much of the shortlist felt like one big mogging contest, with everything competing to be bigger, hotter and more dramatic than whatever came before. Her takeaway for the year is that resilience and a little fun may be the way through. Somewhere, a sourdough loaf is winning.
content_zh:
你整个周末都用在了你朋友身上, 该句现在有一个词典的祝福,因为柯林斯词典已经将2026年的年词命名为"吞吐".

柯林斯将它定义为“表现优异或超越某人或某物,这可能意味着让他们在外表、信心或地位上显得低劣 ” 。 认为这个词对AMOG来说是短的,“群体中的阿尔法男性”。 它于2016年左右在健美文化中开始,在那里它命名了健身房中身体上最占优势的男生,然后变成了动词,并在manosphere进行了轮回.

这也是人们唯一应该使用一个以更衣室啄门为起点的词。 汽车的普及使得柯林斯成为了榜单,他们称之为汽车制造者,用每一个新车型建造更长,更宽,更重的车辆. SUV在2025年的汽车新销量中远超过一半,停车场也感受到了这种感觉.

就业市场为鬼子提供了工作,这是雇主张贴的空缺,没有计划雇用任何人。 柯林斯引用了英国的一项研究 发现大约三分之一的广告角色 符合描述, 所以如果你的申请 不断消失到空虚,

更轻的条目是朋友游戏, 低预算的游戏 与朋友玩, 和fricy,水果加辣, 如菠萝和芒果热酱。 Bixie是Zendaya,Jessie Buckley和Helen Mirren穿戴的波波和精灵之间的发型.

接下来是P(doom),即有人认为AI带来人类文明崩溃的百分率概率,这与理发和热酱一样在同一个列表中找到是一件奇怪的事情. 柯林斯作家瑞秋·昆(英语:Rachel Quin)说,许多入围名单都感觉像是一场大杂耍大赛,一切竞相比以往更大,更热闹,更戏剧化.

她这一年的外卖是 恢复力和一点乐趣 可能是过去的方式。 某处,一个酸面包正在赢得。
author: RELEVANT Staff

title_zh: 德鲁斯基的金钱饥渴的巨型教会牧师正在获得他自己的Netflix系列， 12月1日首映
content: The megachurch pastor Druski has been playing for laughs is getting a promotion. Netflix announced a multiyear deal with the comedian on Nov. 2, and the first project is Collect & Praise, a semi-scripted series built around that character. It premieres Dec. 1. Netflix describes a show where faith comes second to fortune. A money-hungry pastor and his unpredictable deacon scheme their way through scandal, chaos and controversy. Mike Epps plays the deacon. For Druski, the deal is about scale. In the announcement he said Netflix will give him the resources to build on his comedy and reach “a new global audience,” and his company, 4LIFERS Entertainment, will develop original programming for the service. Netflix is also licensing three of his existing projects, Coulda Been Love, Coulda Been Daddy and Coulda Been Records Auditions, along with a selection of his skits. John Derderian, the Netflix VP who oversees Next Gen Content, said Druski “has a gift for building characters that people can’t stop talking about,” and called Collect & Praise “just the beginning.” He started posting skits on Instagram in 2017 and now has nearly 40 million followers across platforms. Along the way he has been a team captain in the Super Bowl LX flag football game, the youngest host in BET Awards history, a TIME100 Next cover star and the top name on Rolling Stone’s list of the most influential creators, all according to Netflix. He has also been to church on screen before, as a co-star of Praise This, the Peacock church musical, and he has appeared in House Party and Livestream from Hell and in music videos for Drake, Jack Harlow and Lil Yachty. RELEVANT last caught him in December, when he and Timothée Chalamet unexpectedly broke into a Kirk Franklin song. He also presented at the NFL Honors, which Netflix says will stream on the service in 2027. Netflix posted an announcement video with the news. Before the series, there is a bigger stage. On Nov. 7, Druski hosts Saturday Night Live, which Netflix says makes him the first digital content creator ever to host the show. The premiere date, Dec. 1, is also Giving Tuesday.

Netflix也为他现有的三个项目颁发许可证, Coulda Been Love, Coulda Been Daddy和Coulda Been Records Experiments,以及他的一些滑稽作品.

监督Next Gen Content的Netflix VP(Netflix VP)John Derderian表示, 德鲁斯基“有造就人物的天赋, 他在2017年开始在Instagram上发布滑板,现在跨平台有近4000万追随者.

他曾经是超级碗LX旗下足球赛的队长,是BET奖历史上最年轻的东道主,是Time100的下一位封面明星,也是滚石最有影响力的创造者名单上的顶级名人,都根据Netflix.

他还在NFL荣誉赛上亮相,Netflix表示将在2027年上线服务. Netflix发布公告视频与新闻. 在系列之前,有一个更大的舞台. 11月7日,德鲁斯基主持周六晚间直播,Netflix称这让他成为有史以来第一个主持节目的数字内容创作者. 12月1日的首映日也是周二

title: Ally Yost: Your Worth Was Never Up for Debate
summary: For a long time, I thought my worth was something other people could give me—or take away. If someone chose me, loved me, complimented me, or told me I mattered, I felt valuable. If someone rejected me, betrayed me, or made me feel replaceable, I began to wonder what was wrong with me. I didn’t…
summary_zh: 长久以来,我一直认为自己的价值是别人可以给我的东西——或者带走的东西。 如果有人选择我,爱我,赞美我,或告诉我我很重要,我感到有价值. 如果有人拒绝我,背叛我,或让我觉得可以替代,我开始怀疑我有什么问题. 我没有...
title_zh: Ally Yost ：你的价值从来没有被辩论过
content: For a long time, I thought my worth was something other people could give me—or take away. If someone chose me, loved me, complimented me, or told me I mattered, I felt valuable. If someone rejected me, betrayed me, or made me feel replaceable, I began to wonder what was wrong with me. I didn’t realize how exhausting it was to live that way until I looked back at the patterns in my relationships. When trust was broken, I didn’t just grieve the relationship. I questioned myself. Was I not enough? Had I become boring? Was I somehow less lovable than the person someone chose instead? Rejection became more than a painful experience; it felt like evidence in a case against my worth. I know I’m not the only person who has done this. Maybe you’ve stayed too long in a relationship because being chosen felt like proof that you mattered. Maybe you’ve replayed a conversation, a breakup, or someone’s silence, trying to figure out what you could have done differently. Or maybe you’ve built a version of yourself that seems confident on the outside but still needs constant reassurance that you’re enough. It’s easy to let other people become the mirrors we use to see ourselves. The problem is that people are inconsistent. Their opinions change. Their attention shifts. Even someone who genuinely loves us can’t be responsible for defining us. When we build our identity on what other people think, we end up handing them a job they were never meant to do. I learned this in a particularly public way when my social media presence began to grow. I could spend hours reading comments, taking in every word as if it had the authority to tell me who I was. Positive comments made me feel beautiful, important, and impactful. Then I’d scroll a little farther and find criticism, and suddenly I was questioning my appearance, my choices, and whether anything I was doing mattered at all. The same person could feel on top of the world one minute and completely torn down the next—all because of a stranger’s opinion. Even praise can become an unstable foundation when we need it to tell us who we are. The issue wasn’t simply that some people were unkind. It was that I had given people’s reactions too much power over my identity. I was looking for a lasting answer in something that could change by the hour. At the time, I thought I needed to become more impressive, more secure, or more successful. But underneath all of that was a deeper question: Where could I find an identity that wouldn’t keep shifting? I had tried to find it in relationships, achievement, attention, and the approval of other people. None of those things could carry the weight I was placing on them. My answer began to change when I encountered Jesus in a personal way. I had grown up around Christianity, but knowing about God and understanding His love for me were two different things. As I began to read the Bible and understand the gospel, I started to see that God’s love wasn’t a reward I had to earn by being good enough. It was a love He chose to give. That truth challenged the way I understood worth. So much of the world’s logic tells us that love is something we earn: be attractive enough, successful enough, easy enough to love, and perhaps you’ll be chosen. But the gospel begins somewhere else. First John 4:19 says, “We love because he first loved us.” God’s love comes before our performance. I didn’t have to make myself worthy of His attention. Jesus had already shown me the depth of His love through His sacrifice. This didn’t mean every insecurity disappeared overnight. I still had to notice how quickly I reached for approval and how easily criticism could take over my thoughts. But I was learning to ask a different question. Instead of asking, “What do they think of me?” I could ask, “What am I building my identity on?” Instead of treating rejection as a verdict, I could remember that another person’s decision did not have the authority to define my value. That distinction matters because

content: Shelf Life , a new comedy from the producers of The Promised Land , follows a pastor who loses his pulpit and ends up working at a grocery store. Jim O’Heir ( Parks and Recreation ) and Zachary Levi ( Shazam! ) lead the cast, and the series is set to premiere exclusively on the Angel platform in 2027. Shelf Life is created, written and directed by Brian Cates and produced by Milk & Honey Studios. It is currently in production. The premise is a former pastor who is kicked out of the pulpit takes a job at a local grocery store, where he realizes his calling to care for others can’t be shelved while surrounded by quirky coworkers. The cast also includes Wesam Keesh, Donna Biscoe, Tommy Woodard, Jonathan Charles, Leilany Celeste, Jazelle Villanueva and Brittany Visser. Richie Johns produces. Mitch Hudson, an executive producer on the series, shared the news on Instagram. “It’s official – I’m executive producing a comedy series starring Jim O’Heir and Zachary Levi!” he wrote. He said Cates has “an incredible vision” as creator and director, that his business partner Johns is leading the producing team, and that Milk & Honey Studios is adding “another comedy show to our lineup” with Angel as a partner. “More info coming soon!” he added. Cates said he has spent 20 years working in the faith and comedy space and believes “if you make people laugh, you can make people listen.” He described the show as something families can watch together, “genuinely funny, but also honest about life, faith, failure and second chances.” The message, he said, is that “we all reach moments when we think we’ve passed our expiration date. But God isn’t finished with us yet.” O’Heir said that with Shelf Life “you come for the laughs, but you end up genuinely caring about these people.”

title: Lauren Daigle Has Released Christmas Music, So the Holiday Season Is Officially Open
summary: Every November, somewhere in a secure facility, a team of professionals gently thaws Mariah Carey so she can sing “All I Want for Christmas Is You” for the entire planet. Christian music has its own version of this tradition, and her name is Lauren Daigle. While nobody has to thaw her—she’s been out here the whole…
summary_zh: 每年11月，在一个安全设施的某个地方，一个专业团队会温柔地解冻Mariah Carey ，这样她就可以为整个星球唱“All I Want for Christmas Is You”。基督教音乐有自己的传统，她的名字叫劳伦·戴格尔（ Lauren Daigle ）。虽然没有人需要解冻她，但她一直在这里……
title_zh: Lauren Daigle发布圣诞音乐，圣诞季正式开放
content: Every November, somewhere in a secure facility, a team of professionals gently thaws Mariah Carey so she can sing “All I Want for Christmas Is You” for the entire planet. Christian music has its own version of this tradition, and her name is Lauren Daigle. While nobody has to thaw her—she’s been out here the whole time—this weekend she released two more holiday songs, this time with the Preservation Hall Jazz Band: “Sleigh Ride” and “Go Tell It on the Mountain.” If you feel like it is too early for this, please know that the paperwork has been filed. Halloween is over, the candy has been marked down to 50 percent, and the Christmas music season has legally begun. For anyone keeping score at home, this is not a new hobby for her. Daigle’s first Christmas album, Behold , came out in 2016 and climbed to No. 29 on the Billboard 200. It also started a tradition: the Behold Christmas Tour, which returns this December for its 10th annual run. That is the real Mariah comparison. A holiday arrives, and so does Lauren Daigle, with a setlist and a very good coat. The new songs are a pair of old favorites with a New Orleans accent. “Sleigh Ride” is the one that has been running through department stores since before you were born, and “Go Tell It on the Mountain” is the spiritual that has been spreading the Good News even longer than that. Preservation Hall brings the brass, the swing, and the general feeling that a very good party has broken out in a church basement. They also joined her last December for a holiday medley at the CMA Country Christmas special, so the chemistry was already on the record. There is also a business angle, if you like those. It is her first release on Capitol, Interscope and CCMG, which is a lot of letters to put on one sleigh. The songs will come out on a 7-inch vinyl on Nov. 27, the day after Thanksgiving, so you can be a person who owns a Christmas record while also being a person who is still full of pie. And if recorded music is not enough, the 10th annual Behold Christmas Tour opens Dec. 2 at the Ryman in Nashville, with stops in New Orleans and Orlando to follow. It is a beautiful room that was built for exactly this kind of evening, and it will probably smell like cinnamon candles and good intentions. The thaw has happened, the songs are out, and the season has officially been declared open. Please enjoy your holidays responsibly, which in this case means having “Sleigh Ride” on rotation.
content_zh:
每年11月,在一个安全的设施里,一群专业人士轻轻地解冻了Mariah Carey,这样她就能为整个地球唱出“我渴望的只有你”。 基督教音乐有它自己的这种传统版本,她叫劳伦·戴格.

这个周末她又发行了两首节日歌曲, 如果你觉得现在为时尚早,请知道文件已经归档。

万圣节结束,糖果被标记为50%,圣诞音乐季合法开始. 对于任何在家记分的人来说,这不是她的新爱好. Daigle的首张圣诞专辑"Beye"于2016年出道并登上"Billboard 200"的29号. 它也开创了传统: 圣诞之旅,

这是真正的Mariah比较。 节日到来 Lauren Daigle也来了 里面有固定名单 外衣很好看 新歌是一对有"新奥尔良口音"的旧相声. " 雪橇骑 " 是自你出生前就一直在百货公司跑来跑去的一款,而 " 在山上说吧 " 是传播 " 好消息 " 的时间甚至更长的精神。

保存 霍尔带来了青铜器,秋千,以及一般感觉一个非常好的聚会在教堂地下室爆发了. 他们去年12月也加入她,参加CMA乡村圣诞特辑会的节日梅德利会,因此化学已经录制了. 也有一个商业角度,如果你喜欢这些。

这是她首次在Capitol,Interscope和CCMG上发布,这是许多要放上雪橇的信. 歌曲会在感恩节后第二天的11月27日以7英寸的花花筒出道,这样你就可以成为拥有圣诞唱片的人,同时也是仍然充满了派的人. 如果录制的音乐还不够的话,第10届年度"看圣诞之旅"(Book Christmas Tour)将于12月开通.

2个在纳什维尔的雷曼车站,在新奥尔良和奥兰多停站后再跟进. 这是一个美丽的房间, 建造的正是这种夜晚, 它可能闻起来像肉桂蜡烛和良好意图。 冰冻已出,歌曲已出道,赛季正式宣布开播.

请以负责任的方式享受假期,这意味着轮回“雪橇骑”。

title: Inside Indie Tribe’s Plan to Disrupt Christian Hip-Hop
summary: On 'Who Do You Say I Am?', the Christian hip-hop collective reads the Bible's villains with empathy — and asks the church to do the same for everyone it writes off.
summary_zh: 在《你说我是谁？》（ Who Do You Say I Am? ）一文中，这位基督教嘻哈乐队以同理心解读了《圣经》中的恶棍，并要求教会为它所注销的每一个人做同样的事情。
title_zh: 探索独立部落颠覆基督教嘻哈的计划
content: Somewhere in the middle of talking about Scripture, Indie Tribe starts arguing about how to describe someone getting kicked in the groin. nobigdyl., Jon Keith, Mogli the Iceburg and DJ Mykael V are mid-sentence about the theological weight of community when the conversation collapses into a bit about their bandmate, Torey D’Shaun, who has stepped out and, per group tradition, is simply “in the bathroom.” The jokes runs a full minute before anyone remembers what they were talking about. This is more or less Indie Tribe’s operating system: theology, friendship, music and dumb jokes occupying the same room. Their new album, Who Do You Say I Am? , works the same way. They didn’t set out to make a concept record. nobigdyl., Jon Keith, Mogli and Mykael V have been a unit for years, joined more recently by D’Shaun, who folded into the group in 2024 in the middle of an album cycle. Their process has never looked like a studio session. It looks like a household. “We live together and eat together, pray together, we do Bible studies, all that kind of stuff, and we make music for a week,” Jon Keith says. They don’t start with a concept. They start with proximity, then look back at what they made and find the thread already running through it. “We kind of look at the range of the songs that we’re making,” Jon Keith says. “We’re like, ‘Okay, it kind of feels like God is moving this in a certain direction.’” Who Do You Say I Am? happened that way. Written and recorded in December 2024 and released March 27 this year, it’s the first project to feature D’Shaun from the ground up, and the group says his arrival changed the chemistry entirely. “This is really the first time to me that it feels like — I love our previous albums, but the way that this album has a heart and a story to it and a concept, it makes the other albums feel like mixtapes,” Jon Keith says. “This joint is easily the longest album we’ve done. It really feels like our first album album.” The title eventually gave them the question holding the record together: What does it actually feel like to be the person history remembers as the villain? “It’s the product of a lot of introspection that we’ve had,” Mogli says. “We’ve gone through the Bible together multiple times through different lenses, at different times in life when we’re going through different things.” The goal wasn’t to defend bad behavior. It was to stop flattening biblical figures into cautionary tales and start reading them like people, asking how it feels to be the character everyone’s quick to condemn. nobigdyl. pushes it further. The discomfort people feel toward Scripture’s messier figures, he argues, says more about a failure of imagination than a failure of faith. title_zh: 本周日，全球教会将为面临严重迫害的3.88亿基督徒祈祷
content: Congregations around the world will set aside Sunday, Nov. 1 for the International Day of Prayer for the Persecuted Church, and this year Open Doors, the Christian ministry that tracks persecution, is asking them to start with Syria. Its 2026 World Watch List moved Syria from 18th place to sixth, a 12-point jump in its score and the largest in the top 10. Open Doors says Syria is now at its most dangerous for Christians since the Islamic State group occupied significant parts of the country. About 300,000 Christians live in Syria. Since the fall of the Assad government in December 2024, the country has been mostly controlled by forces led by Hay’at Tahrir al-Sham, an Islamic extremist group with roots in al-Qaeda. The group has made overtures toward moderation and held talks with representatives of Syria’s traditional Christian communities, but it is too soon to know what will come of the new leadership. Widespread instability has produced deadly clashes that have affected Druze and Alawites in particular, with Christians caught in the crossfire, and Islamic State attacks have resumed, including the deadly attack on a church in Damascus in June 2025. “The trauma of what happened hit us all hard,” said “Mourad,” who is responsible for the work of Open Doors’ local partner in Syria. “We thought getting rid of the previous regime would give us some sense of freedom, yet it seems there are still people who only believe in killing.” The interim Syrian constitution adopted in March 2025 makes Islamic law the main source of legislation, and it offers insufficient protection for religious minorities. Pressure on Christians is greatest in Damascus and Aleppo, while the northeast is generally safer. The World Watch List ranks the 50 countries where Christians face the most extreme persecution, using a points system built on data from experts on the ground in 100 countries. North Korea is first with a score of 97 out of 100, followed by Somalia, Yemen, Sudan and Eritrea. Syria is sixth with 90, ahead of Nigeria, Pakistan, Libya and Iran. Open Doors counts more than 388 million Christians worldwide facing high levels of persecution and discrimination for their faith, about one in seven, and in the top 50 countries alone, more than 315 million face very high or extreme persecution. In its 2026 report it recorded 4,849 Christians killed, 4,712 detained and 3,632 churches and Christian properties attacked. For more than 1,600 years Christians have set aside early November to remember believers who suffered for their faith. Open Doors’ free toolkit for churches and small groups includes guided prayer points, videos, sermon material and social images, and this year’s focus is the Middle East, beginning with Syria. Open Doors’ prayer points for Syria ask for three things: that believers would lean on God as their “Rock eternal” (Isaiah 26:4), that converts from Islam would find love and fellowship even when family and friends reject them, and that the victims of the Damascus church attack would feel God’s closeness.
content_zh: 世界范围内的教会将预留11月1日为受迫害教会国际祈祷日, 今年追踪迫害的基督教部也要求他们从叙利亚开始。 其2026年世界观察榜将叙利亚从第18名提升到第6名,比分跳出12分,位列前10名. 叙利亚现在对基督徒来说是最危险的, 约30万基督徒居住在叙利亚. 自2024年12月阿萨德政府倒台后,该国多由伊斯兰极端主义团体"基地"(Hay'at Tahrir al-Sham)所领导的势力所控制. 这个团体向着温和的态度,并与叙利亚传统基督教社区的代表举行了会谈,但现在还不知道新领导人会怎样。 普遍的不稳定导致了致命的冲突,尤其影响到德鲁兹人和阿拉维人,基督徒陷入了交火中,伊斯兰国又恢复了袭击,包括2025年6月大马士革一教堂被致命袭击. Mourad对叙利亚当地合作伙伴的工作负责。 “我们认为摆脱前政权会给我们一些自由感, 2025年3月通过的叙利亚临时宪法将伊斯兰法作为立法的主要来源,对宗教少数群体的保护不足. 大马士革和阿勒颇对基督徒的压力最大,而东北部一般比较安全. 世界观察列表将基督徒面临最极端迫害的50个国家排行榜,使用基于100个国家当地专家数据建立的分数系统. 朝鲜以97胜100负的分数排名第一,其次是索马里,也门,苏丹和厄立特里亚. 叙利亚以90分位列第六,领先尼日利亚,巴基斯坦,利比亚和伊朗. 开放门人数超过3.88亿,全世界因信仰而面临严重迫害和歧视的基督教徒约有七分之一,仅在前50个国家,就有3.15亿多基督教徒面临极高或极端迫害。 它在2026年的报告中记录了4 849名基督徒被杀死,4 712人被拘押,3 632所教堂和基督教财产被袭击。 1600多年以来,基督徒在11月上旬留作纪念因信仰而受苦受难的信徒. 开放的门对教堂和小团体免费的工具包包括导游的祈祷要点、录像、布道材料和社会形象,今年的重点是中东,首先是叙利亚。 开放的门对叙利亚的祈祷点要求三件事:信徒们倚靠上帝作为他们的"永生"(Isaiah 26:4),从伊斯兰教皈依的人即使家人和朋友拒绝也会找到爱和友谊,大马士革教堂袭击的受害者也会感受到上帝的亲切.

content: Abstract : Jonathan Leeman highlights the corporate component of conversion, pointing out that God not only reconciles us to himself through Christ but also to one another. While our (vertical) reconciliation to God is foundational and primary, our (horizontal) reconciliation to others is necessarily bound up with our salvation. Conversion makes us part of God’s people, and this corporate aspect of our salvation should compel us to join a local church. Editor’s Note: This article is taken from Church Matters, the 9Marks journal for pastors, in the issue titled Conversion . If your doctrine of conversion is missing the corporate element, it’s missing something essential. Jesus died for a people (see Mark 10:45). He saves us as individuals, and he saves us into a people. Salvation includes a family. If you’re not convinced, jump straight to these parallel statements from Peter: Once you were not a people, but now you are God’s people; once you had not received mercy, but now you have received mercy. (1 Pet. 2:10) If someone asks you how you became a Christian, you probably emphasize the second line in your testimony. You say something like, “I was living in sin apart from God. A friend shared the gospel with me. I recognized who God is and what Christ did in dying and rising again. Therefore, I repented and believed. Praise God, he forgave me and I received his mercy!” What a wonderful testimony. Don’t stop saying that! Widen Your Perspective But notice that Peter widens the aperture of the camera and tells us a little more about what happened in that same moment. In addition to moving from not mercy to mercy, we simultaneously moved from not a people to a people. That means our testimonies could include a little bit more. Like this: “I was living in sin apart from God, and I wanted nothing to do with God’s family, the church. A friend shared the gospel with me. I recognized who God is and what Christ did in dying and rising again. Therefore, I repented and believed. Praise God, he forgave me and I received his mercy! I also realized that—wow!—I was part of a family now, the church.” Do you see what I mean by the “corporate” component of conversion? We’re saved into the universal church. That’s not to say we should put the corporate element out front. One might think of N. T. Wright’s well-known line about justification being “not so much about soteriology as about ecclesiology; not so much about salvation as about the church . ” N.T. Wright, What Saint Paul Really Said (Eerdmans, 20 1 4), 1 1 9. This is a clear example, in Douglas Moo’s almost-as-well-known line, of backgrounding what the New Testament foregrounds, and foregrounding what the New Testament backgrounds (as cited in D. A. Carson, “Faith and Faithfulness,” Ligonier, February 1 , 20 1 0, https://learn.ligonier.org/articles/faith-and-faithfulness). There can be no true reconciliation between humans until individual sinners are first reconciled to God. The horizontal necessarily follows the vertical. Ecclesiology necessarily follows soteriology. Which is to say, the corporate element must not come first, lest we lose salvation altogether. Vertical and Horizontal But it must come. Indeed, the corporate component must remain within the structure of the doctrine of conversion itself. Our corporate unity in Christ is not just an implication of conversion; it’s part of the very thing. Being reconciled to God’s people is distinct from but inseparable from being reconciled to God. These two elements of conversion are wonderfully put on display in Ephesians 2 with two instances of the word “but.” The first comes as Paul narrates man’s rescue from sin and death (vv. 1–10), which hinges on the words “ But God, being rich in mercy . . . ” (v. 4). Those words introduce God’s saving love and the fact that he has “raised us up with [Christ] and seated us with him in the heavenly places in Christ Jesus” (v. 6). title: Help for Beginners and Seasoned Preachers: A Review of David Jackman’s From Text to Teaching
summary: Seeing preaching as a science helps us understand that there are tools we can apply to do the work better. Seeing it as an art reminds us that the work requires us to pay attention to the beauty of Bible proclamation.   The post  Help for Beginners and Seasoned Preachers: A Review of David Jackman’s From Text to Teaching  appeared first on  9Marks .
summary_zh: 将讲道视为一门科学有助于我们理解，我们可以运用一些工具来更好地完成工作。把它看作一门艺术提醒我们，这件作品需要我们关注圣经宣讲的美丽。帮助初学者和经验丰富的传教士：大卫·杰克曼（ David Jackman ）的《从文本到教学》（ From Text to Teaching ）一文首先出现在9Marks上。
title_zh: 初学者和经验丰富的传教士的帮助：大卫·杰克曼从文本到教学的回顾
content: Abstract: Jeremy Meeks reviews David Jackman’s From Text to Teaching: A Guide to Preparing Bible Talks and commends it as a helpful resource for anyone who preaches or teaches the Bible in any context. This brief book offers discussions of the art and science of preaching and the process of preparation, and it provides an inside look at Jackman’s own preparation to preach 1 Corinthians 1–4. The final chapters offer checklists that will be practically useful for preachers, and the appendix contains the author’s own template for preparing a Bible talk. Both beginners and seasoned preachers and teachers will benefit from this book. David Jackman, From Text to Teaching: A Guide to Preparing Bible Talks . Matthias Media, 2021. 92 pp. Even seasoned preacher needs to go back to basics sometimes and be refreshed. Similarly, guys starting out need instruction—someone to teach them how to go about the craft. Often the most helpful teachers are those who have lots of experience. What is even better is if such a preacher has also spent substantial time training others to preach. Ideally, that preacher/trainer has such command of the material that he is able to distill his insights and counsel into a tight, readable book. We have been given such a gift in David Jackman’s little volume From Text to Teaching . In just 92 pages, Jackman provides a lifetime of wisdom for the beginner and the seasoned preacher alike. As he explains in the introduction, he is addressing (as evidenced in the title) the skill of Bible teaching more generally and not solely preaching. This might turn away preachers who don’t consider themselves to be giving “Bible talks,” but that would be the preacher’s loss. The weight of what we get to do every time we open the Bible and teach from it in any context is rightly esteemed by Jackman. The Art and Science of Preaching The book begins by discussing the “Art and Science of Preaching.” Both aspects of preaching—art and science—must be held onto if we are to do it well. Seeing preaching as a science helps us understand that there are tools we can apply to do the work better. Seeing it as an art reminds us that the work requires us to pay attention to the beauty of Bible proclamation. Preaching is more than using the Bible to communicate. Rather, our task is to preach what the text says, that is, giving the meaning of what it says, in context, for the people sitting in front of us. Jackman’s convictions will be new to some, common to others, but beneficial to all. The Process of Preparation A substantial chapter is dedicated to the “Process of Preparation”. Here Jackman helps the Bible preacher/teacher think through how to put a message together. As a preacher who trains other preachers, I’m constantly asked how I do this on a weekly basis, and I enjoy hearing how others do it as well. Jackman has sage advice. He reminds us that we should always be praying (an obvious but seriously neglected aspect of preparation). He is also clear that we should use the time we have strategically. We never have as much time as we would like, and we often think we need more time than we do. The fact is that preachers often waste a lot of time because they are not strategic. Jackman recommends setting aside a few blocks of time in the week (four sessions that are each two to three hours). What is vital is that the preacher figures out what works well for him and plans his schedule accordingly. Jackman then gives helpful advice on how to go about studying and writing out the sermon inside those blocks of time, and this advice is helpful for those at all levels of proficiency. Invited into the Author’s Study The next three chapters (3–5) of the book are pure gold. In essence, Jackman invites us into his study to listen in as he walks through his process of preparing messages on 1 Corinthians 1–4. Here we get insights into how his suggested process works in actual texts. This is something many books on preaching neglect to do, leaving the rea

摘要:杰里米·米克(Jeremy Meeks)评论了大卫·杰克曼的"从文字到教学:准备圣经谈话的指南",并称赞它是任何背景中宣扬或教授圣经的人的有用资源. 这本简短的书提供了对布道的艺术和科学以及准备过程的讨论,它提供了杰克曼自己为布道1科林斯1–4的准备的内观.

最后的章节提供了对传道者实际上有用的核对表,附录中包含了作者自己准备圣经演讲的模板. 初学者和老练的传道人和教师都将受益于这本书。 David Jackman,《从文字到教学:准备圣经会谈指南》,Matthias Media,2021年。

甚至老练的传教士有时也需要回到基础,被刷新. 类似地,开始的人需要教书,有人教他们如何操作这款工艺。 最有帮助的教师往往是经验丰富的教师。 更好的是,如果这种传道者也花大量时间训练其他人传道。

理想的情况是,传教士/教官对材料有如此高的指挥力,他能够将自己的见解和咨询意见提炼成一本紧凑可读的书。 在大卫·杰克曼的"从文字到教学"一书中,我们得到了这样的礼物。 在92页里,杰克曼为初学者和老练的传道者提供了一生的智慧.

正如他在导言中所解释的,他正在讨论(如标题所证明的)《圣经》教学的技巧更普遍,而不仅仅是传道。 这可能会让那些不认为自己在进行“圣经会谈”的传道者退后,

每当我们打开圣经并在任何背景中从中教导时,我们所能做的事情的分量都得到了杰克曼的正确尊重. 该书首先讨论了“影响艺术与科学”。 如果我们要做得好,就必须坚持艺术和科学两个方面的传道。

将传道视为一种科学,有助于我们理解,我们可以应用一些工具来更好地开展工作。 把它看作是一门艺术,提醒我们,这部作品需要我们关注"圣经"宣言的美. 意义不仅仅是用"圣经"来沟通.

相反,我们的任务是宣扬案文所说的话,即在背景上赋予案文所述的含义,供坐在我们前面的人民使用。 杰克曼的信念对一些人来说是新的,对另一些人来说是共同的,但对所有人都有好处。 1. 编写过程

在这里,杰克曼帮助"圣经"的传道人/老师思考如何将一个信息集中起来. 作为一名培养其他传教士的传教士, 我经常问每周我怎么做, 杰克曼有圣人的建议 他提醒我们,我们应当永远祈祷(准备工作中一个明显但被严重忽略的方面)。

他还明确指出,我们应该从战略角度利用我们的时间。 我们从来没有像我们想要的那样多的时间,我们常常认为我们需要比我们多的时间。 事实是道教经常会因为不具有战略意义而浪费大量时间. 杰克曼建议在一周内留出几块时间(每两到三小时四会).

重要的是,传道者要知道什么对他很有效,并据此规划他的时间安排。 杰克曼随后就如何研究并写出这些时间段内的布道给出了有益的建议,而这个建议对于所有水平的熟练程度的人都是有帮助的. 书中接下来的三章(3–5)是纯金.

基本上,杰克曼邀请我们进入他的书房 在他行走的过程中聆听 他准备了科林斯1 -4的信息。 在这里,我们深入了解他建议的进程如何在实际文本中发挥作用。 这是很多书 关于布道 忽略做,留下的灵性

title: Discerning Between Godly and Worldly Grief
summary: Godly grief leads to mourning over sin, not simply its consequences.   The post  Discerning Between Godly and Worldly Grief  appeared first on  9Marks .
summary_zh: 敬虔的悲伤会导致对罪的哀悼，而不仅仅是对罪的后果的哀悼。文章《辨别虔诚与世俗的悲伤》首次出现在九分榜上。
title_zh: 分辨虔诚与世俗的悲伤
content: Abstract: Sam Crites offers three ways to help pastors distinguish between worldly grief and godly grief based on Paul’s words in 2 Corinthians 7:10. Only godly grief produces true repentance, and such grief can be discerned by mourning over sin, not merely its consequences; a genuine desire for reconciliation, no matter the cost; and an earnest desire to please God, not the world. The fruit of godly grief usually becomes evident over time through ongoing repentance and faith in Christ. Editor’s Note: This article is taken from Church Matters, the 9Marks journal for pastors, in the issue titled Conversion . I was discipled by a man named Steve Tucker. He was a simple man full of simple lessons, and one of those simple lessons has stuck with me: a true mark of genuine conversion and its effects is how willing someone is to repent of their sin. However, genuine repentance is a tricky thing. When I catch my children doing something wrong, they are more than willing to “repent,” especially when punishment is imminent. They go from enjoying their wrongdoing to shedding tears. But it’s not always easy to tell if they are grieved over upsetting me or because they know there will be consequences for their actions. Pastors have to make a similar determination when a member is confronted for their sin. Is this person shedding tears only because they were caught in sin, or are they truly repenting? Both kinds of grief can look the same, at least on the surface, but only one leads to life. Those who refuse to repent give evidence that they haven’t been converted. So how can we tell the difference? Three Marks of Godly Grief Since we cannot see the heart of a man, we must look at the fruit of his life—the marks of repentance that accompany genuine conversion. Heart change, not behavior modification, is always the aim. Therefore, we must discern the external evidences of the Spirit’s internal work. This is where Paul’s words to the Corinthians can help us out. He says, “For godly grief produces a repentance that leads to salvation without regret, whereas worldly grief produces death” (2 Cor. 7:10). Notice that genuine repentance is produced by “godly grief.” Allow me, then, to put forward three marks of repentance from 2 Corinthians 7 that are evidence of godly grief. This list is not meant to be exhaustive but merely a helpful tool for discerning true repentance and, therefore, genuine conversion. 1. Godly Grief Leads to Mourning over Sin, Not Simply Its Consequences In 2 Corinthians 7, Paul describes how restless and anxious he was as he awaited the Corinthians’ response to his previous letter. But when Titus came, Paul was comforted because his report brought news of the grief of the Corinthians—not grief over the harshness of Paul’s letter but grief over their own sin. We’re reminded that godly grief is first and foremost a response to sin and not merely its consequences. David says to God in Psalm 51:4, “Against you, you only, have I sinned and done what is evil in your sight.” How could David be so insensitive? What about Uriah and Bathsheba? Or the child who died? David was aware of how the consequences of his sin affected others, but he felt greater anguish in his heart over how he had offended the Lord. And this should be true for all who repent: they should care most about how their sin has offended their Lord. This is the fruit of understanding the gospel, as the sufferings of Christ on the cross were the payment due for our sin. On the other hand, a preoccupation with the sin of others, a tendency to shift the blame to someone else, or grief that is only short-lived—all these are indications that an individual is not mourning because they have offended the Lord, but instead because of the consequences of their sin. 2. Godly Grief Leads to a Genuine Desire for Reconciliation, No Matter the Cost The Corinthians were grieved that their sin had ruptured their relationship with Paul.
